## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. [Method](../method.md)

## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (ollaya-f32, needs 10.9 GB, NVIDIA only, from [github.com/ollaya-dev](https://github.com/ollaya-dev/ollaya/blob/9b8698e39f11a0f0bcd08ad686de51cd1b4f6fa8/results/runs/2026-10-24-latency-rtx5090-cuda-d3.json))
   
   ```sh
   ollaya run d3:mini --preset triage "The customer requests a refund."
   ```

[Download model files](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-mini/tree/df99bf4ca4418bc6908ee68e9b7479af1f3b8800) · Published model files verified. This is a verified repository snapshot; the benchmark does not establish an identical weight revision. A matching Ollaya runtime manifest and published short-workload GPU memory measurement were reviewed separately; see local variants and identity\_note. The command was not executed in this review.
